To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a combination of US+NUs subsampling strategies allows for reducing the amount of streamed power data, without compromising the disaggregation performance.

1) the use of NUS sampling strategy allows for reducing the data rate of a factor of 5, while achieving disaggregation performance comparable to OS and US sampling; 2) the combination of NUS and US sampling strategy allows for achieving disaggregation performance better than OS and US sampling and comparable to NUS sampling, while reducing the data rate by a factor of 10.

a) a data reduction strategy based on the combination of US and NUS allows for obtaining disaggregation performance superior to the ones obtained with the use of original sampled data and with a data reduction of 50% and b) the combination of US with NUS allows to obtain disaggregation performance similar to the ones obtained by using original sampled data, with an average data reduction of 75%.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel approach for NILM, based on the adoption of a data reduction strategy, which allows for preserving disaggregation performance, and for achieving a reduction in the amount of acquired data and the computational burden of the device.

the definition of an ad hoc sampling scheme for the disaggregation process, which can be easily implemented on the device side, and allows for reducing the amount of streamed and elaborated data without affecting the disaggregation performance, and, thus, the reliability of the system.
the definition of a data reduction strategy that allows for preserving the disaggregation performance while reducing the amount of data to be streamed and processed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NUS+US strategy allows for reducing the data rate by 90%, with a negligible impact on the disaggregation quality.
the NUS strategy is able to achieve the best trade-off between disaggregation performance and data reduction.
, in terms of NILM disaggregation accuracy, the NUS scheme outperforms both the US and OS strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of NILM applications, the use of non-uniform subsampled data, together with a Deep Learning based disaggregation technique, allows to achieve a performance comparable to the one obtained using the original data, but reducing the amount of data by a factor of up to 10.

the use of a NUS scheme, in conjunction with a Deep Learning based disaggregation technique, is a promising approach for NILM systems, allowing for a reliable disaggregation process with a reduced data acquisition and elaboration load.

the proposed data reduction scheme can be applied to the aggregate signal without any significant loss in disaggregation accuracy, thus allowing for a reduction of the data stream and the computational resources of the device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper subsampling strategy, together with an appropriate disaggregation algorithm, can be a good compromise between data reduction and disaggregation performance.

the proposed NUS strategy, in combination with US sampling, allows for reducing the data acquisition and elaboration effort of a NILM device, and, consequently, its power consumption, without compromising the disaggregation performance.
a non-uniform sampling strategy can be effectively exploited for data reduction purposes without affecting disaggregation performance.
